_metadata.title: Exhaustive pair manifest for the approved 50-word shortlist
_metadata.assignments: plannedBatch is assigned once and never changes on later runs
_metadata.note: bestAvailableCandidate is the strongest non-playable hint, kept separate from playable eligibility; it is never published automatically

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: Apple tree is direct; bears climb trees but tree does not point at bear on its own.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: apple tree is instant and a bear in a tree is familiar imagery, the least strained second side

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: White Castle is a familiar chain; apple only through Snow White's apple.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: White Castle gives one certain side and Snow White gives a real if indirect route to apple

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: Gala is a top-selling apple variety; crown only via royalty attending a gala.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: the apple variety is a real foothold and formal galas at least evoke crowns

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: Ice cold nearly renames ice; apple has no cold sense.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: ice is certain and a crisp cold apple is the least implausible second side on offer

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: Candy apple is direct; king only via king-size candy bars, which does not point at king.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: candy apple is certain and king-size candy is at least a phrase containing king

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: Knight in shining armor is direct; a shining polished apple is a weak descriptor link.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: the only hint with any path to apple while nailing knight

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: Aslan the lion is well known; the apple of youth in The Magician's Nephew is deep-cut trivia.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: the only hint with any genuine apple reference, however obscure

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: Atlantic Ocean is direct; the Big Apple sitting on the Atlantic coast is too thin to count.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: ocean is certain and New York's Atlantic coast is the only thread, however thin, toward the Big Apple

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: Ringtone is direct; tone does not reach apple.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: ringtone is certain and the iPhone's default ringtone is the faintest thread to Apple

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: Apple tree is direct; trees cast shadows but tree does not point at shadow.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: the only hint with any path to shadow while nailing apple

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: Apple crate is a familiar object, but crates reach TRAIN only via generic freight hauling.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: The only hint with a real foothold on both words, even though the TRAIN side is generic freight.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: Bank account is a compound and a ghost account (abandoned or fake account) is a reasonably familiar phrase.
bestAvailableCandidate.heldReason: override: 'ghost account' is a specialist phrase: best-available stretch for BANK+GHOST, not a confident general-US hint.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: The only hint where both sides are set phrases, even if 'ghost account' is less universal.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: Horse stable is direct; a 'stable bank' is an adjective use a player may not connect.
Iron bar is direct; gold bars in a bank is an inferred image and there is no 'bank bar' phrase.
Bank vault is direct; a key for the vault is an inferred detail.
A bank ATM is immediate and the automated teller is machine-like, but ROBOT is implied rather than recognized.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: The automated-machine idea is the only real bridge offered to ROBOT.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: The Congress Avenue Bridge bat colony in Austin is a real shared scene, but a player who does not know it has no route to either word.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: Only hint; valid fact, but the scene is regional knowledge.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: A dental crown gives TOOTH to CROWN, but bats' teeth are not a recognizable association for BAT.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: Only hint; one-sided.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: Honey is made from nectar; some bats are nectar-feeding pollinators, a true fact that many players will not hold.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: Only hint; honest fact but the bat side is specialist knowledge.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: Vampire bat is immediate; the only route to HORSE is that vampire bats feed on livestock, which no player will reach.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: Only hint; effectively bat-only.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: Secret key is a phrase; BAT is reached only by a rescue explanation about Batman's secret identity or secret Batcave.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: Only hint; key-only.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: Vampire bat is immediate; KING is reached only through Dracula as 'king of the vampires', a loose characterisation rather than a set phrase.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: Only hint; the king side is thin.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: Bat cave is immediate; lions are pictured in dens and on rocks rather than caves, and the 'cave lion' is an extinct species few know.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: Only hint; the lion side is a stretch.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: Bats fly; MOUSE is reached only through the idea that a bat is a 'flying mouse', which uses the other target to get there.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: Only hint; the pair-as-one-creature idea is cute but mouse alone is not reached.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: Rays swim in the ocean; the 'bat ray' is a real species but far too specialist for a player to reach BAT.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: Only hint; ocean-only in practice.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: Bats are drawn black and pirates fly the black flag (Blackbeard), but colour alone points at many words.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: Only hint; both sides reachable but by colour only.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: Vampire bat is immediate; QUEEN is reached only through 'Queen of the Damned' / vampire-queen fiction, which is niche.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: Only hint; the queen side needs genre knowledge.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: RING is reached as a near-synonym (a ring is a circle); BAT only via the loose verb image of bats circling overhead, which few players would land on.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: Only hint offered; RING side is solid but the BAT side is a weak verb image.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: BAT via vampire bats drinking blood; ROSE only via the colour phrase 'blood-red rose', a mood/colour link.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: Reaches BAT strongly and ROSE via a familiar colour phrase; the only hint with any two-sidedness.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: WATER via skimming stones or skimming the water's surface; BAT via bats skimming low over water to drink or catch insects, a true but little-known behaviour.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: Only hint; WATER is reached easily but the bat behaviour is a naturalist's fact rather than common knowledge.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: BEAR via hiking in bear country; BELL via the bear bell hikers wear to warn bears off, a scene known mainly to outdoors people.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: The bear-bell hiking scene genuinely joins both words, but only hikers will see the BELL side quickly.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: BEAR via Paddington Bear; CROWN via Paddington's tea with the Queen for the Platinum Jubilee and the Paddington tributes after her death, a largely British memory.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: Only hint; the royal link is real and affectionate but not what most players carry for Paddington.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: GHOST via spirit as a synonym; BEAR via the spirit bear (Kermode) or the bear as a spirit animal, both a stretch for a general player.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: Only hint; the bear side exists (spirit bear, spirit animal) but is not what SPIRIT evokes.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: BEAR via the bear hug; HEART only via hugs as a gesture of love, a mood association rather than a scene or phrase.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: Bear hug is universal and hug-to-heart is an easy emotional step, though not a definite route.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: KEY via the wind-up key; BEAR via the wind-up toy bear, which exists but is not the first wind-up toy players picture.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: Only hint; the wind-up toy scene is coherent but the bear is incidental to it.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: KNIGHT via a knight's armour; BEAR only via the armoured bears of His Dark Materials, which most players will not reach.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: Only hint; functionally one-sided for anyone who has not read Pullman.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: LIGHT via the Northern Lights; BEAR via the polar bear of the far north and the Great Bear in the northern sky, neither a set phrase.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: The Arctic scene (aurora over polar bears) is familiar, but BEAR has no compound with NORTHERN.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: BEAR via polar bear; NIGHT via the 'polar night' of the Arctic winter, a real term that many players will not know.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: Only hint; bear side is immediate and polar night is a genuine compound, just not a common one.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: Bear cave is solid, but shadow reaches cave only through darkness-as-mood or Plato's shadows on the cave wall, which few players will summon from the word alone.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: The only hint that reaches the bear; the shadow side is a dim mood link rather than a phrase or scene.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: Bells toll, but ghost is reached only through a death-knell mood with no phrase, story or scene that a player would name.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: Only hint offered; it reaches bell strongly and ghost only as atmosphere.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: Sweet is almost a definition of honey, while bell is reached only through sweet bell pepper or the sweet sound of bells, neither of which a player will land on from the word alone.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: Only hint offered; it reaches honey trivially and bell only by a side door.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: Ice cream is instant, but cream reaches bell only via the ice-cream van's chime, which routes through the other target rather than the hint word.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: Only hint offered; the ice-cream-van bell is a real scene but needs ICE already solved to see it.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: Bell tower is a compound, but king reaches tower only through castle imagery or the chess rook, neither a phrase a player would volunteer.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: Only hint offered; strong on bell, loose on king.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: Knights and castles go together instantly, but a castle bell is not a stock phrase; church towers, not castles, are where players place bells.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: Only hint offered; the knight side is strong and a castle bell is at least plausible.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: Tinker Bell is immediate, and she appears as a darting light in Peter Pan, but light is reached only through the character, i.e. via the other target.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: Only hint offered; the character does carry both ideas if the player knows she is shown as a glowing light.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: Circus lion is instant, but there is no recognizable circus bell; the ringmaster uses a whistle and a boxing bell is a different venue.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: Only hint offered; it does not reach the bell.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: Belle and the enchanted rose (Beauty and the Beast) is a fine rose route, but BELLE contains and is essentially a spelling variant of the target BELL, a rule failure.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: If the contains-target rule were waived, Belle's rose is a genuine story link; THORN never reaches BELL at all.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: Bell tower is a strong compound, but the shadow side is only 'a tower casts a long shadow', which any tall object does.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: Only hint offered; the bell-tower half is strong and the shadow half is plausible if not specific.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: Rattlesnake is direct, but bells jingle rather than rattle; the bell side depends on a baby rattle with bells or jingle bells 'rattling', which is a stretch.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: Only hint offered; the snake side is excellent and the bell side is reachable via a bell rattle toy.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: Bell tower is strong, but nothing recognizable connects a spider to a tower (the nursery spider climbs a water spout, not a tower), so this is one-sided.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: Only hint offered; it does not reach SPIDER and should not be served.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: Witches and candles are a familiar ritual image, and 'bell, book and candle' (the witchcraft/exorcism phrase and film) ties bell to candle, but that phrase is not widely known enough to call the bell side clear.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: The bell-book-and-candle phrase genuinely binds all three ideas, so a knowing player gets both; BROOM reaches only the witch.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: Cracking an egg is direct, but a cracked bridge is just structural damage that could apply to any object, so the bridge side is not specific.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: Only hint offered; egg side is perfect and a cracked concrete bridge is at least a plausible image.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: Toll bridge is direct, but ghost is reached only by a two-step invention (bell tolls for the dead, the dead become ghosts), which is a rescue explanation.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: Only hint offered; it does not reach GHOST and should not be served.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: Dental bridge is direct; honey is reached only via 'sweet tooth', which is not a compound with honey.
Toll bridge is direct, but 'kings levied tolls' is a historical explanation invented to rescue the word; no player sees king from toll.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: Only hint offered; it does not reach KING and should not be served.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: Guardian lion statues are a strong image and stone lions do flank famous bridges, but statue alone does not clearly point at a bridge for most players.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: Only hint offered; the lion-statues-at-the-bridgehead scene is real but the bridge side is secondary.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: A bridge is a crossing, but nothing recognizable links a mouse to crossing, so this is one-sided filler.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: Only hint offered; it does not reach MOUSE and should not be served.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: Bay Bridge reaches BRIDGE; SHARK is reached only through sharks sighted in a bay or the Australian place-name Shark Bay, neither of which a player would name readily.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: Only hint; the shark half is a thin coastal association rather than a shared scene.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: Suspension bridge is the obvious compound for BRIDGE; a spider hanging suspended on its thread, or webs likened to suspension bridges, reaches SPIDER only with some reconstruction.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: Only hint; the spider half is a plausible image but not a phrase anyone uses.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: Bridge over a river reaches BRIDGE; WITCH is reached only via witch-ducking in rivers, a historical detail players would not recall from the word RIVER.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: Only hint, and the witch half is effectively missing.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: A bridge crossing is a direct compound for BRIDGE; WOLF is reached only through wildlife-crossing signs or Red Riding Hood crossing the woods, neither of which names a wolf.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: Only hint; the wolf half is a weak animal-crossing association.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: Mickey Mouse makes the mouse side immediate, but the card side only reaches via Disney gift cards or the niche Lorcana trading-card game.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: Only hint offered; mouse side is excellent but card is a weak afterthought.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: Ocean's Eleven is a well-known casino film, but the card side only reaches through the casino setting or an ace counting eleven in blackjack.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: Only hint offered; the casino-heist setting gives card a thin but real foothold.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: Card trick is immediate, but shadow only reaches via hand-shadow puppetry or 'a trick of the light'.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: Only hint offered; shadow puppets as a trick is thin but imaginable.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: Card dealer is immediate, but nothing recognizable links dealer to snake (snake-oil goes with 'salesman', not 'dealer').
bestAvailableCandidate.why: Only hint offered; it does not reach snake.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: Ace is the top card, and ace and star are both words for a top performer, a shared-meaning route that is defensible but not a phrase.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: Reaches card perfectly and star through the shared 'top performer' sense, which is more natural than TRADING's picture-on-the-card route.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: Train ticket is immediate; card only follows because a ticket is a small printed card or a travel card replaces one.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: Only hint offered; the card-as-ticket route is plausible but not a familiar phrase.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: Puss is a cat (Puss in Boots), but castle only reaches via the ogre's castle Puss wins in the tale, a detail most players do not retain.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: Only hint offered; cat is certain and the fairy-tale setting gives castle a faint foothold.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: Humpty Dumpty is the egg; castle only arrives through the wall and the king's horses and men, which illustrations sometimes set at a castle.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: Only hint offered; egg is certain, castle is an inference from the rhyme's royal setting.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: Mead is honey wine drunk in medieval castle halls, but many players will not know what mead is made from and the castle link is only a mood.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: Only hint offered; correct on both sides but niche.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: A beacon is a signal light, but castle only reaches through beacon fires lit on castle towers, an image many players will not produce.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: Only hint offered; light is certain, castle is a tower-signal inference.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: Reaches CASTLE only through the phrase/film 'castle in the sky' while MOON is simply something in the sky; the castle side is a phrase a player may not land on.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: Only hint offered; the moon side is immediate and 'castle in the sky' is a known phrase, so it is a fair stretch rather than filler.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: A moat is unmistakably castle; it reaches RING only through the shape idea that a moat rings the castle, which a player must reconstruct.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: Only hint; the ring-shaped-moat route is real but a shape stretch rather than a named connection.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: Sea salt is a compound for SALT, but the castle side relies only on castles standing by the sea (or sandcastles), which is not a named route.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: Only hint; the salt side is a compound, the castle side is scenery.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: A tower is a castle part, but reaching SHADOW requires inventing 'a tall tower casts a shadow', which is not a recognizable connection.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: Only hint; serves the castle side only.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: A dungeon is castle through and through, but snakes in a dungeon is a looser pit trope than cobwebs or rats; the snake side needs the player to imagine it.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: Only hint; castle side is certain and the snake-pit image is plausible.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: Castle gardens and gardens blooming in spring are both real, but neither side is a direct route; GARDEN points at many things before either target.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: Only hint; both sides are soft associations.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: Cat's-eye is a compound for CAT, but EYE reaches DIAMOND only via 'cat's-eye is also a gemstone', an explanation invented to rescue the diamond side.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: Only hint; serves the cat side only.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: Purr is pure cat; there is no familiar phrase or scene linking purring to HEART beyond a vague 'warms the heart' explanation.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: Only hint; serves the cat side only.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: Cats lick themselves and their paws for CAT; honey is licked off a spoon or paw for HONEY, but that side is a verb applicable to any food.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: Only hint; verb route is real but the honey side is weak.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: Black cat is a strong compound for CAT; the iron side rests on cast/wrought iron being black, a colour association rather than a named route.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: Only hint; cat side certain, iron side is a colour association.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: Puss is simply another word for cat; KNIGHT is reached only by casting Puss in Boots as a sword-wielding hero, who is a swashbuckler rather than a knight.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: Only hint; the Puss in Boots hero image is the sole knight route.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: Cat's tail is direct, but ring reaches tail only through 'ring-tailed' (lemur, ringtail cat), a phrase a player would not recover from TAIL alone.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: Only hint offered; it is one-sided but the only candidate.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: Crown-king is direct; the dog side rests on 'King' as a common dog name and the King Charles spaniel, which a player may not land on.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: King Charles spaniel and the dog name 'King' give it a slightly firmer dog foothold than ROYAL.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: Faberge eggs are famous; the crown side is that they were made for the Russian imperial crown (the Tsars) and are jewelled like crowns, which many players know only vaguely.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: Only hint; the imperial-egg link is real and moderately known.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: 'Ring of fire' is a familiar phrase; a crown is a ring-shaped circlet of jewellery, but a player is unlikely to move from RING to CROWN without prompting.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: The only hint with a plausible, if thin, route to both (ring of fire; crown as a ring).

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: Queen to crown is immediate; honey needs queen bee and then the hive, two steps.
The Statue of Liberty's spiked crown is iconic; light comes only through her torch and that is a second step.
Crown-king is direct; the mouse side is the Mouse King of The Nutcracker, known mainly to ballet audiences.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: Only hint; the Nutcracker's Mouse King is a real but moderate route.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: Salt tax is a well-known historical compound (gabelle, Salt March); taxes are paid to the Crown, but TAX does not point at CROWN clearly.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: Salt tax is a real compound and the Crown is the historical tax collector; the most concrete of three stretches.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: The crown of a tree is a real but moderately known term; trees cast shadows, though 'shade' is the more natural word.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: The only hint that touches both words (tree crown; tree shadow), even if each touch is light.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: Crown Jewels is immediate; the 'jewel spider' is an obscure species name and gives no recognizable route to SPIDER.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: Only hint offered; it is CROWN-only filler and should not be served.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: Stars shine by definition; a crown is shiny, but shining is not a defining property of CROWN the way sweetness is of an apple.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: Only hint; shared-property route that is strong for STAR and secondary for CROWN.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: A cap is headwear akin to a crown and 'crown cap' is the bottle-cap term; the cap of a water bottle reaches WATER, but both sides are one step removed.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: Only hint; bottle cap touches both (crown cap / water bottle cap) but neither word is immediate.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: Alpha wolf is a familiar compound; the CROWN side is only the metaphor alpha = leader = the one who wears the crown.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: Only hint; strong for WOLF, metaphorical for CROWN.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: Fish scales are immediate; diamonds are weighed on a jeweller's scales (carats), a plausible but not instant second sense.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: Only hint; double meaning touches both but the DIAMOND side is secondary.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: Cursed diamonds (Hope Diamond) and curses bringing ghosts are each a stretch.
Rock is slang for a diamond; LION is reached only via Pride Rock in The Lion King or lions on a rock, a scene most players will not jump to from ROCK alone.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: Only hint; strong for DIAMOND, story-dependent for LION.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: A mouse is the archetypal tiny animal; diamonds are small but TINY is not a defining property of a diamond.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: Only hint; shared size property that is strong for MOUSE and weak for DIAMOND.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: Diamond is the proverbial hardest substance; a robot is only loosely hard (rigid metal body, hard-wired), so the robot side leans on a weak material property.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: Only hint offered; the diamond side is unmistakable and a player can reach a metal robot through 'hard' with some effort.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: The 'diamond ring' effect of a total solar eclipse is real but specialist knowledge, while an eclipse is literally the moon's shadow.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: Shadow side is solid and the diamond-ring effect is at least a genuine, nameable fact for astronomy-aware players.

pairs.generationHold: owner found BACK indirect (reached it via the Arizona Diamondbacks); PATTERN and SCALE are held borderline, so the pair has no clean TREASURE-level hint. Future generation hold only: the live beta-01-002 snapshot and completed history stay exactly as they are.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: Dew beading on a spider web is a recognisable scene and dewdrops are poetically called diamonds, but each side only works once the player already pictures the web.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: Only hint; the dew-jewelled web is a genuine shared image even if neither word is reached directly.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: The Wicked Witch covets the slippers in The Wizard of Oz, but they are ruby (silver in the book), never diamond, so the diamond side rests on a wrong fact.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: Only hint offered; it reaches WITCH but has no honest path to DIAMOND.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: Wolf fang is immediate; there is no recognised diamond route (diamond-studded grillz is not a familiar 'fang' scene).
bestAvailableCandidate.why: Only hint offered; it is wolf-only filler.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: Toothless is the dragon in How to Train Your Dragon, famously written to behave like a big puppy; the dog side depends on knowing that characterisation (or an old toothless dog).
bestAvailableCandidate.why: Dragon side is a named character; the puppy-like behaviour is a genuine shared trait for anyone who knows the films.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: Sweetie and honey are interchangeable endearments (and honey is sweet); the dog side is only that people call their dogs sweetie, which applies to any pet or person.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: Only hint offered; honey side is solid, dog side is a fond-owner stretch.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: 'Sit' is the first dog command; no recognisable key route exists (a 'sit' key, dog-sitting with a house key, and sitting at piano keys are all invented).
bestAvailableCandidate.why: Only hint offered; it is dog-only filler.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: The mane is the lion's signature; only a few dog breeds (chow, Tibetan mastiff, the lion-cut Pomeranian) are described as maned.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: Lion side is iconic and maned dog breeds give a thin but real dog route.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: A spring bounces by definition; a bouncy, excited dog is a real image but far from the first thing BOUNCE suggests.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: The only legal hint here; the springy, bouncing dog is a plausible if soft route.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: Dragons get slain, but SLAIN has no route to HEART.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: The only legal hint, though it reaches only the dragon side.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: Dragon fruit is a familiar compound, but FRUIT only reaches HONEY via a loose natural-sweetener or honeydew association.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: Dragon fruit is solid and honey at least sits in the same sweet-food space.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: Dragons guard hoards, but GUARD does not lead to KEY without inventing a guarded key.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: Marginally better: a dragon guarding something a key opens is at least an imaginable scene.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: A lunar eclipse is a moon event, and East Asian myth says a dragon swallows the moon to cause it, but most Western players will not know that.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: At least rests on a real dragon myth, unlike NIGHT.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: Mushu is Mulan's dragon, but his being small is not a route to MOUSE; the Disney-mouse link is an invented rescue.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: A real dragon reference whose tiny size at least gestures toward mouse-scale.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: Mecha are giant robots in anime, and mecha-dragons exist in games (Mecha Dragon, Mechagodzilla-style), but both halves are genre knowledge.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: At least a real genre where robot dragons appear.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: St George slew the dragon, and the red rose is worn on St George's Day as England's flower, but the rose side is English custom few others know.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: A genuine dragon reference with a real, if regional, rose link.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: Key lime is a compound; egg is reached only via key lime pie being made with yolks, which no player would see.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: If forced, LIME at least rests on a true two-sided fact (key lime pie uses egg yolks); EASTER has nothing on the key side.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: Humpty Dumpty is the egg; knight only via 'all the king's men' standing in for knights (or the White Knight nearby in Through the Looking-Glass), a stretch.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: The rhyme's king's men and the castle-wall setting give a weak but real medieval route; SHELL has none.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: Lions live in zoos; nothing reaches egg.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: Neither works; ZOO is marginally less hopeless because zoos do display hatching eggs, but it remains one-sided.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: Night owl is a compound; owl reaches egg only as 'a bird that lays eggs'.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: Night owl is a strong compound and an owl at least lays eggs; NOG has no night side at all.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: Pirate treasure is immediate; egg only via the Easter egg hunt being a kind of treasure hunt.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: Egg hunt as treasure hunt is a shared activity, a better egg route than 'birds lay eggs'.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: Onion ring; egg only via the batter, which is not a route a player sees.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: Neither works; ONION at least has egg-and-onion as a familiar food pairing behind it, whereas YOLK has no ring side.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: Salt and pepper is the fixed pair; egg only as the breakfast plate they are shaken over.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: Salt-and-pepper-on-eggs is a real breakfast scene, giving the most recognisable egg side of the three.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: Candlelight throws shadows; egg only via the niche practice of candling eggs.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: The only hint with any egg side at all, even if candling is niche.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: A 'mermaid's purse' is a shark egg case: a genuine two-sided link but niche natural-history knowledge.
bestAvailableCandidate.why: The only hint whose connection actually involves both egg and shark, even though it is niche.

bestAvailableCandidate.reason: Dining car; egg only as a thing one eats.
